CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Centre
Department of Haematology and Oncology Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL DETAILS
Reason for Referral: New diagnosis of likely acute leukaemia
Clinical History: Patient presents with pancytopenia and circulating blasts. Bone marrow aspirate shows 45% myeloblasts with Auer rods. Flow cytometry pending.

TEST PERFORMED
1. Conventional Cytogenetics - G-banding analysis
2. Interphase FISH analysis for RUNX1-RUNX1T1 rearrangement

SPECIMEN TYPE: Bone marrow aspirate

RESULTS

CONVENTIONAL CYTOGENETICS
Method: G-banding analysis at 400-550 band resolution
Culture conditions: 24 and 48 hour unstimulated cultures
Number of cells analyzed: 10 metaphases

Karyotype: 46,XY,t(8;21)(q22;q22)[5]/46,idem,del(9)(q13q22)[5]

ABNORMAL RESULT
- Translocation between chromosomes 8q22 and 21q22 detected in 5/10 cells (50%)
- Clonal evolution with t(8;21) and additional deletion of 9q (q13 to q22) in 5/10 cells (50%)
- No normal metaphases identified

INTERPHASE FISH ANALYSIS
Probe: RUNX1-RUNX1T1 Dual Fusion Translocation Probe (Abbott Molecular)
Number of cells scored: 100 interphase nuclei

Result: nuc ish(RUNX1T1,RUNX1)x2(RUNX1T1 con RUNX1x2)[61/100]

ABNORMAL - Positive for RUNX1-RUNX1T1 rearrangement
- 61/100 cells (61%) show fusion signal pattern consistent with t(8;21)
- 39/100 cells (39%) show normal signal pattern

INTERPRETATION
The cytogenetic analysis reveals an abnormal karyotype with a balanced translocation between chromosomes 8 and 21 at breakpoints q22, characteristic of the t(8;21)(q22;q22) rearrangement. This translocation results in the RUNX1-RUNX1T1 (formerly AML1-ETO) fusion gene, which was confirmed by interphase FISH analysis in 61% of cells examined.

Additionally, clonal evolution is evident with 50% of metaphases showing an interstitial deletion of the long arm of chromosome 9 from bands q13 to q22 in addition to the t(8;21). The del(9q) is a known secondary karyotypic abnormality associated with t(8;21) rearrangement.

The t(8;21)(q22;q22) is one of the most common recurring chromosomal abnormalities in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), occurring in approximately 5-10% of cases. This translocation is associated with AML with maturation (FAB-M2) and is classified as a favorable cytogenetic risk factor according to current risk stratification systems. Patients with t(8;21) AML generally have a good response to standard chemotherapy regimens, though the presence of additional cytogenetic abnormalities such as del(9q) may impact prognosis.

The RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusion protein acts as an aberrant transcription factor that blocks normal myeloid differentiation. This genetic alteration is considered a Class II mutation in AML pathogenesis and often occurs with additional mutations affecting signal transduction pathways.

CLINICAL CORRELATION
These cytogenetic findings are consistent with the clinical diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia. The t(8;21) is a recognized finding in AML and classified as good cytogenetic risk factor. The presence of the secondary del(9q) abnormality is commonly seen with t(8;21) and its prognostic significance remains under investigation.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Reviewed by: [redacted name], MD, PhD
